answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents mint stake-backed cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Each trusted transaction acts as an inlet funneling reputation into a river of verified interactions, turning valid activity into a clear signal. Sybil swarms face exponential capital exhaustion, as creating n coordinated identities imposes a superlinear O(2^n) deposit cost, rendering mass spoofing economically unviable.
